objective: Correct the cruush 1.6 Spots experience shown in Julien's Android screenshots: restore useful Spot filters, open directly into the board, add 7-day and no-expiry board posts, move secondary details below the board, enlarge the mobile Spot header, remove redundant helper copy, and remove the nonfunctional Discover button.
userOutcome: A member can find the right Spot quickly and reach its board immediately, with useful post lifetimes and no decorative steps blocking the board.
audience: Authenticated cruush members using Spots on Android mobile and desktop.
successCriteria: The Spots drawer shows its search, sort, distance, activity, place-type, and existing public Spot-tag filters directly without a Discover mode button.
Filters alter both drawer results and the default Spot map layer using existing server-backed fields only.

Selecting a Spot opens its board immediately. The board and Who's Here switcher appears directly below the compact Spot identity block, before description, ratings, Popular times, source, and other secondary details.
Board posts offer 1h, 3h, 6h, 12h, 24h, 7d, and Never. A separate Who's Here duration appears only when the member opts into Who's Here.
The primary board action says Post to board.
The non-embedded Spot detail header has a larger Android-mobile touch and title area.
Redundant helper lines beneath the Add Spot controls are removed while required privacy and safety meaning remains intact.
No Discover button remains in the Spots drawer.
mustPreserve: Preserve the approved cruush vector map style and every non-Spots map behavior.
Preserve current Crowd Mode behavior and add no Crowd Mode menu or demographic Spot filter.
Preserve Spot search, five sorts, publishing, suggestions, ratings, reports, Popular times, board encryption, physical-distance checks, Who's Here opt-in, deletion, and pagination.
Preserve all unrelated user work and the exact existing icon assets.
nonGoals: No Crowd Mode changes, inferred demographic data, fabricated Spot vibes, or fake feature availability.
No test creation or test execution.
No server restart, migration execution, push, deployment, changelog edit, or email work.
